title: Schedule temporal reevaluation with durable resource and attention budgets
summary: Provide scheduling and budget primitives for assessment, investigation, and attention. Clock changes can matter without new evidence, but idle timers must not repeatedly call semantic evaluators or flood catch-up notices.
implementation: Persist timer scope, rule versions, dependencies, firing identity, and cancellation epoch.
Implement due-condition processing with scheduled/actual time and coalesced catch-up.
Provide independent resource and attention reservation ledgers with expiry and release.
Trigger only affected temporal outputs and reuse unchanged semantics; trusted controls bypass this queue.

acceptance.criterion: Deadline crossing updates attention without rerunning unchanged semantic support.
acceptance.verification: Advance a fake clock and inspect evaluator invocation counts.

acceptance.criterion: Concurrent workers cannot exceed one shared remaining budget.
acceptance.verification: Race reservations across connections and audit committed totals.

acceptance.criterion: Restart catches up once per current condition without obsolete periodic warning floods.
acceptance.verification: Advance across downtime and inspect firing identities.

tests: Cancelled timers remain inert after restart.
Late firing records delay rather than rewriting schedule.
Stop applies despite exhausted ordinary budgets.
risks: Independent per-rule counters can overspend global budgets under concurrency.

reuse.application: Express boundedness and temporal triggers through shared deterministic primitives.

evidence: 2026-10-27: Durable generation-bound timers and atomic resource/attention allocations enforce current controls, replay, bounded catch-up and conservative charging. Actual acceptance evidence and limitations: docs/validation/MAT-020.md.
